deliverables.title: Mandate, stakeholders and service envelope
deliverables.acceptance: Named scope, beneficiaries, exclusions, demand and accountable service owner.

deliverables.title: Requirement applicability and acceptance allocation
deliverables.acceptance: Every selected baseline requirement has applicability, owner, design home and verification method.

deliverables.title: High-level physical, logical and security views
deliverables.acceptance: Components, connections, trust/authority/failure boundaries, data paths and assumptions are coherent.

deliverables.title: Architecture decisions and allowed variations
deliverables.acceptance: Alternatives, rationale, consequences, affected requirements and actual decision authority recorded.

deliverables.title: Threat, co-residency and control responsibility
deliverables.acceptance: Sharing at each layer, credible failures/compromises, residual risks and inherited controls are assigned.

deliverables.title: Availability, recovery, capacity and location strategy
deliverables.acceptance: Offered service boundaries and objectives are separated from categorization; exit and recovery constraints explicit.

deliverables.title: Vendor realization and provisioning strategy
deliverables.acceptance: Native realization choices and P0–P6 responsibilities are linked without assuming one universal provider.

deliverables.title: Architecture review and engineering handoff
deliverables.acceptance: Critical design decisions resolved or blocked by scope; signed disposition and engineering inputs available.

deliverables.title: Site LLD and controlled design release
deliverables.acceptance: Actual values and source references replace examples; reviewed topology and controlled revision identified.

deliverables.title: Physical inventory, bill of materials and port/cable schedule
deliverables.acceptance: Hardware/optic/firmware/power dependencies, rack and link endpoints, support and staging accepted.

deliverables.title: Network, addressing, routes and ZIP paths
deliverables.acceptance: Forward/reply routes, service endpoints, enforcement, MTU and alternate paths recorded per family.

deliverables.title: Compute, storage and placement schedules
deliverables.acceptance: Eligible hosts, native placement, virtual disk/data paths, copies and recovery membership are explicit.

deliverables.title: Management, shared-service and trust interfaces
deliverables.acceptance: Consumption/admin separation, initiating clients, role/key scope and bootstrap/recovery dependencies mapped.

deliverables.title: Capacity, performance, MTU and failure calculations
deliverables.acceptance: Assumptions and measured survivor capacity share units and failure basis; all bottlenecks evaluated.

deliverables.title: Exact stack and operation-level automation coverage
deliverables.acceptance: Products, APIs, providers, installers, hardware, entitlements and all lifecycle operations have a support disposition.

deliverables.title: Build, rollback and qualification design
deliverables.acceptance: Site-specific MOP, rollback/forward repair, test resources and assertion coverage reviewed before execution.

deliverables.title: Engineering release and implementation handoff
deliverables.acceptance: Versioned design, artifacts, credentials references, evidence plan and unresolved blockers handed over explicitly.

deliverables.title: Change scope, release freeze and execution authority
deliverables.acceptance: Actual change reference, immutable artifacts, scope, participants and stop authority recorded.

deliverables.title: Staging and installation readiness
deliverables.acceptance: Supplier/asset checks, approved installation method, facility work, recovery access and staging results accepted.

deliverables.title: P0–P1 bootstrap and foundation receipts
deliverables.acceptance: Trusted independent access, minimum services and verified physical/network transport precede platform consumption.

deliverables.title: P2 native platform build receipts
deliverables.acceptance: Installer and native resource changes match approved tuple; APIs, baseline and supported recovery observed.

deliverables.title: P3 shared-service and boundary receipts
deliverables.acceptance: Denied boundary paths, service clients, return routing, names/trust/backup and management separation observed.

deliverables.title: Restricted qualification fixture and test campaign
deliverables.acceptance: Authorized disposable scope, actual observations and supporting control paths; no production qualification assumed.

deliverables.title: G4 initial operational and recovery readiness
deliverables.acceptance: Owners, support, monitoring, incident paths and required restore/recovery evidence accepted before activation.

deliverables.title: P4–P5 tenant build and production activation
deliverables.acceptance: G0/G1/G2, applicable initial G4, current tests and valid authority precede reversible activation.

deliverables.title: As-built, defect and evidence records
deliverables.acceptance: Actual identities, configurations, departures, tests, evidence and owner acceptance are attributable.

deliverables.title: P6 maintenance, migration and retirement
deliverables.acceptance: Change requalification, fencing, retained-copy/key obligations, access withdrawal and safe disposal tracked.

views.question: What service is offered and who owns each external dependency?
views.required_content: Sites, tenants, provider services, consumers, external authorities.

views.question: Where are the equipment, links, power and shared failure dependencies?
views.required_content: Sites/racks, cells, OOB, host pools, storage, edges, control components.

views.question: Which independent authorities and zones exist?
views.required_content: Tenant/WSD/domain/instance/network, owner, sharing and trust transitions.

views.question: Where do request and reply travel and where are they enforced?
views.required_content: Gateways, ZIPs, allowed prefixes, routes, NAT, policy and native bypass candidates.

views.question: Who can change each component and by which protected path?
views.required_content: Privileged endpoint, management domain, roles, API/BMC, break-glass and logging.

views.question: Which resources and copies share hardware/control and how is placement enforced?
views.required_content: Pools, schedulers, virtual disks, file/object clients, copies, keys and protection.

views.question: What is the consumer allowed to do and how does the service reply?
views.required_content: Service endpoint, client identity, return routes, backend authorization and admin plane.

views.question: Which failures are covered and which dependencies must survive?
views.required_content: Failure sets, quorum/fencing, independent trust, restored service scope and failback.

views.question: Which native components realize the same requirements on each selected stack?
views.required_content: Actual tuple, mechanisms, enforcement locations, support limits and alternatives.

views.question: What is installed, allocated, changed and retired by each owner?
views.required_content: P0–P6 resources, prerequisites, single-writer ownership, handoffs and safe stops.

views.question: How does the current environment become and remain the target?
views.required_content: Adoption waves, dependencies, capacity, operating responsibilities, exit and disposal.

requirements.text: The hosting contract SHALL be vendor neutral and SHALL NOT require consumers to specify vendor-specific identifiers or topology objects.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Routine tenant and workload lifecycle operations SHOULD NOT require changes to physical leaf or spine configuration.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: All inter-zone paths SHALL be explicit and SHALL traverse the applicable ZIP/security edge.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Management/OOB traffic SHALL be separated from tenant operational traffic and SHALL have independently controlled access paths.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Every implementation SHALL publish its offered service classes, supported information categories, excluded capabilities and required qualification evidence before accepting a production request.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Tenant identity, security-zone identity, workload lifecycle, and platform realization are separate concepts.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: A VPC, VRF, Tier-1 gateway, or Neutron router is an implementation mechanism, not the enterprise definition of a security zone.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Routes are derived from authorized intent; workload owners do not provide arbitrary route tables, BGP peers, route targets, or prefix imports/exports.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Shared services are exposed through explicit service bindings; broad reachability to a common-services supernet is not the default.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Portability means equivalent required outcomes and conformance, not identical topology.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: A deployment is not Service Ready until realized state and security controls are verified.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Failure of an admission or control-plane dependency SHALL fail new changes closed; failure SHALL NOT silently create a security bypass.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: The service contract SHALL remain stable when a supported platform is replaced, provided the replacement platform passes the required conformance profile.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Platform-specific extensions MAY be offered, but they SHALL be declared as capabilities and SHALL NOT redefine the portable core semantics.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Every normative requirement SHALL have a stable identifier, accountable owner, applicability, source basis, verification procedure and exception policy; generated catalogues SHALL contain every active requirement.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Technical conformance, service readiness and formal authorization SHALL be recorded as distinct states; an automated test result SHALL NOT create, renew or impersonate an authorization decision.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: The standards register SHALL record edition, effective/review date, applicability, owner and supersession relationships; external changes SHALL trigger an impact review of affected profiles and evidence.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Control mappings SHALL preserve source edition and identifier and SHALL distinguish direct source requirements, local translations and design decisions; a family-level crosswalk SHALL NOT be represented as a completed control assessment.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Each WSD SHALL record confidentiality, integrity and availability separately and SHALL reference the exact adopted SecurityProfile, AssuranceProfile, AvailabilityProfile, RecoveryProfile and PlacementProfile.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Profile resolution SHALL be immutable and authorized; a consumer SHALL NOT lower mandatory requirements by editing a profile, forging a status field or choosing an unsupported category.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Each platform qualification and material WSD change SHALL include a threat/failure analysis that identifies trust boundaries, privileged actors, dependency failures, residual risks and applicable tests.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Every network SHALL resolve to one Security Domain Instance, one logical domain, one zone class, one address authority and one accountable owner; shared-domain lifecycle SHALL use explicit dependency references.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Provider service consumption, platform control, privileged management and OOB transport SHALL be modeled separately; a shared service SHALL NOT create implicit authority over another plane.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Cross-tenant routing SHALL be denied by default even when two tenants use the same zone class.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Tenant administrators SHALL NOT have authority to modify provider management, security-edge infrastructure, physical fabric, or another tenant namespace.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Tenant ownership, entitlements and role bindings SHALL be versioned and auditable; suspension SHALL specify permitted recovery/containment actions and SHALL NOT imply indiscriminate workload deletion.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Every managed workload SHALL belong to a WSD or an explicitly documented equivalent lifecycle object.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: The WSD SHALL contain security and connectivity intent; it SHALL NOT contain vendor-specific infrastructure identifiers in the consumer contract.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: A WSD SHALL declare compute, storage, identity, backup, recovery, exposure and evidence dependencies in addition to network intent; unresolved mandatory dependencies SHALL block Service Ready.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: A Security Domain Instance SHALL contain only networks authorized to share its routing/security authority.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Sharing a zone class SHALL NOT imply reachability between independent Security Domain Instances.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Dedicated Security Domain Instances SHOULD be available for workloads whose assurance profile or threat model requires stronger isolation than shared logical segmentation.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Each Security Domain Instance SHALL reference a logical domain and a qualified site/platform realization; membership and sharing changes SHALL be assessed as security-significant changes.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Internal instance zoneClass SHALL be limited to PAZ, OZ, RZ, HRZ or provider-controlled MZ; external PZ/REZ relationships SHALL use ExternalDomain with explicit authority and trust metadata.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Every requested adjacency SHALL be evaluated against the versioned zone policy before allocation; being permitted to create a ZIP SHALL NOT grant any traffic by default.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: All inter-zone network paths SHALL traverse the applicable ZIP/security edge.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: A ZIP SHALL identify exactly two authorized adjacent endpoints, each an internal domain instance or approved external/management domain, and SHALL NOT create a general-purpose third-zone transit path.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Default inter-zone policy SHALL be deny; allowed flows SHALL be generated from approved Flow Intentions and Service Bindings.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: ZIP management traffic SHALL be segregated from operational traffic.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Data-path ZIPs and management-path ZIPs SHALL be governed and deployed as distinct security services; shared virtualization SHALL only be used where the applicable assurance analysis supports it.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Each ZIP SHALL record its two zone authorities, joint approval, required security functions, management authority, heightened posture, session-revocation behavior and current evidence.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: A distributed or shared-infrastructure ZIP SHALL be qualified against the same required security outcomes as a dedicated edge; any unsupported mandatory function SHALL make that realization ineligible.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Tenant workload networks SHALL have no direct route to infrastructure management interfaces.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Administrative access SHALL originate from an authorized management access path and traverse management-specific security controls.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Automation identities used to manage tenant workloads SHALL be separated from identities able to modify the physical fabric, security edge, or management foundation.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Break-glass access SHALL be separately controlled, strongly authenticated, logged, time-bounded where feasible, and periodically tested.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: The implementation SHALL document independent MZ semantics, OOB transport dependencies, remote-management boundary and privileged identity controls; tenant-facing APIs SHALL NOT expose infrastructure administration.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: A platform SHALL provide an isolated routing/policy mechanism capable of realizing the Security Domain semantics required by the applicable conformance profile.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Native routing MAY be used within one authorized Security Domain Instance; communication between independent security domains SHALL follow the approved boundary/ZIP realization and its policy.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Before a workload is attached, the adapter SHALL normalize permissive native defaults and enforce the mandatory baseline on all supported NIC, router, gateway and workload-attachment paths.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Routes, route imports/exports, and BGP adjacencies SHALL be provider-controlled outputs of authorized intent.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: A generalized shared transit VRF SHALL NOT be used as a default inter-zone routing mechanism.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Temporary migration or transition routes SHALL have explicit scope, approval, expiry, telemetry, and automated teardown.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Route compilation SHALL validate connected routes, recursive next hops, summaries, NAT/PBR interactions and all enabled address families; realized forwarding SHALL be compared with the approved graph before exposure.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Every managed network SHALL have an authoritative IPAM record and owner.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Overlapping address space SHALL be an explicit exception or migration pattern, not the standard tenancy model.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Address release SHOULD include quarantine/reuse controls appropriate to DNS, logging, firewall state, and incident-response requirements.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Address allocation, DNS/DHCP registration and release SHALL use idempotent operation identities, conflict detection and a dependency-aware quarantine policy; IPAM failure SHALL NOT cause guessed allocations.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Security semantics SHALL be equivalent across IPv4 and IPv6 unless an explicit, approved protocol-specific exception exists.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Conformance testing SHALL include IPv6 negative-path tests before a platform is certified for dual-stack service.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Every offered address-family mode SHALL define local protocol controls, ICMPv6/PMTU treatment, transition-path restrictions and complete service/recovery dependencies; unsupported family combinations SHALL be rejected.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Consumers SHALL NOT receive broad routing to a shared-services supernet solely because they consume one shared service.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Where useful, shared services SHOULD expose zone-aligned endpoints so that consumption does not force unnecessary cross-zone routing.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Each ServiceProfile SHALL define direction, endpoint identity, authentication, allowed scope, availability, failure behavior and management separation; bindings SHALL be revoked when their entitlement or service version expires.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: A workload SHALL NOT obtain direct public ingress by attaching its internal Security Domain directly to a public network.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Public exposure SHALL be represented by an Exposure object with owner, protocol, endpoint, certificate/DNS dependencies, logging, security profile, and lifecycle state.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Internet egress SHALL be deny-by-default and enabled only through an approved egress profile.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Egress telemetry SHALL permit attribution to the originating tenant/WSD and should preserve useful source identity where operationally feasible.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Exposure SHALL remain disabled until current-generation boundary, certificate, backend, logging and authorization gates pass; exposure revocation SHALL enforce the approved existing-session policy.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: WSD-to-WSD and tier-to-tier communication inside a shared Security Domain Instance SHALL be denied unless an approved policy explicitly permits it.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Platform metadata used for security policy SHALL be managed, validated, and protected from unauthorized tenant modification.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: The platform SHALL prevent unapproved NIC, source-identity, privileged-workload and label changes from bypassing mandatory segmentation; effective policy SHALL be verified for same-host and cross-host traffic.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Every domain-to-boundary attachment SHALL have a provider-owned EdgeAttachment record covering forwarding authority, isolation, MTU, HA, capacity and cleanup; consumers SHALL NOT choose its native topology identifiers.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: A shared attachment SHALL be prohibited unless direct connected, neighbor, gateway and NAT/PBR paths preserve the required domain isolation and ZIP enforcement in normal and failure states.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Security Domain Instances SHOULD be site-local by default.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Layer-2 stretch across sites SHALL require a documented application/availability requirement and failure-domain analysis.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Recovery-site connectivity SHALL be pre-authorized and tested; emergency recovery SHALL NOT depend on ad hoc route leaking.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Recovery placement SHALL preserve domain, co-residency, cryptographic, identity and location constraints; writer fencing and failback ownership SHALL be proven before production recovery is offered.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Compute placement, maintenance evacuation, migration and HA restart SHALL enforce the approved tenant/domain/zone co-residency matrix; no scheduler action SHALL silently weaken it.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Each compute profile SHALL define supported hardware/software, boot/attestation controls, administrative isolation, resource guarantees, overcommit policy and handling of unsupported devices.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: The meaning of dedicated compute SHALL state its exact physical and administrative scope and disclose any shared storage, network, control, support or recovery dependency.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Every storage resource and derivative copy SHALL carry owner, categorization, access scope, key policy, placement/retention constraints and lineage; cross-scope attachment or export SHALL require explicit authorization.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Storage service profiles SHALL define measurable capacity/performance, consistency, replication, snapshot/clone and portability semantics and SHALL be tested under contention and the accepted failure condition.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Storage release and reuse SHALL reconcile all known copies and legal/administrative holds, apply an approved sanitization method and retain a receipt describing scope, method, verification and exceptions.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Human, workload and automation identities SHALL have separately scoped authorization, credential lifecycle and accountability; no tenant identity SHALL acquire provider foundation authority through role or group inheritance.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Privileged access SHALL use the approved hardened path, strong authentication, least privilege and time-bound delegation; emergency and supplier access SHALL be logged, tested and revoked after use.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Credential and session revocation SHALL be verified at the consuming service within the approved propagation interval, including cached tokens and delegated grants.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Protected data services SHALL enforce their versioned cryptographic profile at rest and in transit; the profile SHALL identify approved algorithms/modes, endpoint identity validation, module/operating-environment evidence and exceptions.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Key use, administration, recovery and destruction SHALL have explicit separated authority and dependency records; key destruction SHALL NOT invalidate required retained-data recovery without an approved disposition decision.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: KMS/trust-service outage behavior SHALL be tested and SHALL NOT enable plaintext fallback; cryptographic inventory, certificate rotation and algorithm-transition plans SHALL be maintained.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Only approved versioned images and baselines SHALL be deployed; each SHALL include provenance, digest, support status, hardening and vulnerability disposition with a retirement/rebuild policy.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Runtime configuration SHALL be verified against the required baseline after provisioning and material change; unsupported protection agents or disabled mandatory controls SHALL not be silently accepted.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Backup consumers SHALL NOT receive connectivity to backup management interfaces merely because they consume backup service.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Restore workflows SHALL enforce the same tenant, security-zone, identity, and evidence controls as backup ingestion.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Every protected production WSD SHALL have a BackupPolicy with consistency, retention, location, key and protected-copy requirements; successful isolated restore SHALL be demonstrated at the policy cadence.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Production credentials SHALL NOT be able to destroy or reduce the protection of recovery copies designated independent/immutable; retained copies SHALL keep the keys and catalogue required for authorized recovery.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Availability and recovery profiles SHALL define measurement scope, SLO, failure tolerance, maintenance treatment, RTO/RPO, consistency, dependencies and test cadence; impact categorization SHALL NOT substitute for these values.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Recovery/HA capabilities SHALL be measured under the approved load and failure scenario before a platform offers the profile; reported SLOs SHALL disclose exclusions and actual breaches.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Placement SHALL satisfy all mandatory security, assurance, location, lifecycle, capacity and recovery constraints using a current qualified platform profile; unresolved or conflicting constraints SHALL reject the request.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Data, backup, telemetry, diagnostic, control-plane, administrative-access and key locations/control constraints SHALL be represented separately and enforced through approved profiles and agreements.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Each portable service class SHALL have a documented exit path, declared proprietary dependencies and representative export/recovery evidence; residency or format support alone SHALL NOT be presented as portability or sovereignty proof.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: The service catalogue SHALL publish entitlements, hard quotas, reservation semantics, availability/recovery targets, supported capabilities and lifecycle obligations with stable service identifiers.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Capacity inventory SHALL reconcile procured, staged, commissioned, available, reserved and consumed resources and SHALL report unused/stranded capacity, ownership and support-life exposure.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Every applicable infrastructure/application control and recovery dependency SHALL have a provider, tenant or shared responsibility assignment and evidence owner; unresolved mandatory responsibilities SHALL block Service Ready.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Routine create, update and retirement of tenants/WSDs in a precommissioned overlay service class SHALL NOT require leaf/spine configuration changes; foundation growth and fabric-routed service classes SHALL use separately authorized workflows.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: A physical VRF SHALL be created only when the physical fabric itself must provide L3 routing for a legitimate routing/security domain.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: Function names such as backup, migration, platform, ZIP, or generic transit SHALL NOT by themselves justify a VRF.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: The fabric profile SHALL define addressing/routing authority, control-plane protection, MTU, fault convergence, management isolation, maintenance and measured scale before platform commissioning.
requirements.executionStatus: Specified, not executed by this release

requirements.text: When EVPN is used, RD/RT/VNI, gateway and multihoming policies SHALL be provider-owned, collision-checked and domain-scoped; unapproved route imports SHALL be denied.

tests.title: Cross-tenant IPv4 isolation
tests.preconditions: Two authorized test tenants; live endpoints and a same-tenant positive control.
tests.procedure: Probe disallowed TCP/UDP services in both directions, including same-host and different-host placements. Compare platform policy and edge telemetry.
tests.expected: All unapproved flows are denied; positive controls succeed; no misleading pass caused by a dead endpoint.
tests.evidence: Probe results, endpoint health, routing/policy snapshots and attribution.

tests.title: Cross-tenant IPv6 isolation
tests.preconditions: IPv6-qualified test endpoints; both tenants have allocated prefixes.
tests.procedure: Repeat CT-001 over global/unique-local IPv6; inspect link-local exposure at each segment boundary.
tests.expected: Unapproved IPv6 flows are denied without breaking required local IPv6 operation.
tests.evidence: IPv6 probes, neighbor state, policy and deny telemetry.

tests.title: Zone-boundary bypass prevention
tests.preconditions: Two distinct zone domains with one approved test flow.
tests.procedure: Inspect all native, static, policy-based and external-network paths; test same-host, cross-host and shared-attachment cases. Correlate the allowed flow at the declared logical ZIP.
tests.expected: No undeclared path exists; allowed traffic is enforced by the ZIP realization; removing that authorization denies it.
tests.evidence: Topology graph, routes, packet-path or enforcement trace and policy digests.

tests.title: Infrastructure management isolation
tests.preconditions: Inventory of management APIs, BMCs, consoles, storage administration and backup administration.
tests.procedure: From test workloads, attempt the enumerated management endpoints over all enabled families. Separately verify approved management access.
tests.expected: Workloads cannot access infrastructure management; dedicated authorized administration still works.
tests.evidence: Inventory coverage, negative probes and management access audit.

tests.title: Default Internet denial
tests.preconditions: WSD has no egress Exposure; a provider-controlled external test endpoint is available.
tests.procedure: Attempt direct and proxy-mediated external access, including IPv6, alternate DNS and common tunnel paths allowed by the test plan.
tests.expected: No unapproved egress succeeds; no default-route or NAT shortcut defeats policy.
tests.evidence: Route/NAT inventory, probes and egress logs.

tests.title: Public ingress protection
tests.preconditions: Internal test service and a controlled external test client.
tests.procedure: Probe an internal workload directly, then exercise a separately approved PAZ ingress service.
tests.expected: Direct exposure is denied; the approved ingress reaches only its declared backend and port.
tests.evidence: Exposure object, DNS/certificate records and ingress/backend traces.

tests.title: Approved stateful flow
tests.preconditions: Versioned FlowProfile and approved source/destination identities.
tests.procedure: Open the authorized application session and its reply path; test unsolicited reverse sessions and a nearby disallowed service.
tests.expected: Intended request/reply works; reverse initiation is allowed only when separately declared.
tests.evidence: Flow intent, compiled rule and application-level probe results.

tests.title: Service-binding scope
tests.preconditions: One bound and one unbound provider service endpoint.
tests.procedure: Exercise required DNS, time, identity or backup consumption; probe the rest of the service subnet and administrative interface.
tests.expected: Only declared service endpoints/directions are reachable; consuming one service does not expose its subnet or management.
tests.evidence: Binding resolution, probes and service-side attribution.

tests.title: Route-authority integrity
tests.preconditions: Approved route graph and realized routing snapshots.
tests.procedure: Compare imported/exported prefixes, defaults, next hops and BGP neighbors with the compiled plan; check recursive next-hop reachability and summaries.
tests.expected: No unauthorized route or advertisement exists; summaries cannot expose excluded domains.
tests.evidence: Compiler output, RIB/FIB snapshots and semantic diff.

tests.title: Security-event attribution
tests.preconditions: Central collector reachable and time synchronization healthy.
tests.procedure: Generate an allowed and denied flow plus an administrative change; find the correlated records centrally.
tests.expected: Records identify tenant, WSD/domain, policy, actor, timestamp and deployment; timestamps satisfy the logging profile.
tests.evidence: Events, correlation query and collection-delay measurement.

tests.title: Control-plane loss
tests.preconditions: Approved isolated test environment; outage and restoration plan.
tests.procedure: Remove catalogue/controller or platform-management connectivity independently; observe existing enforcement and attempts to provision.
tests.expected: Existing approved paths retain enforcement; new unsafe changes stop; recovery converges without bypass.
tests.evidence: Before/during/after policy snapshots, alerts and operation journal.

tests.title: Security-edge node failure
tests.preconditions: Measured production-like load within the selected profile; spare capacity available.
tests.procedure: Fail one edge node or its uplink under an approved test plan and measure sessions, drops, recovery and policy continuity.
tests.expected: No unauthorized traffic is permitted; recovery and remaining capacity meet the accepted profile.
tests.evidence: Time-series traffic, failover timeline and enforcement traces.

tests.title: Offboarding residuals
tests.preconditions: Disposable WSD, retention policy and resource graph recorded.
tests.procedure: Run retirement; query routes, policy, identities, addresses, DNS, certificates and storage/backup records by stable WSD ID.
tests.expected: Active connectivity and grants are removed; retained copies are explicitly owned/locked; the tombstone explains every remaining object.
tests.evidence: Deletion ledger, scans, retention receipts and sanitization references.

tests.title: Security drift detection
tests.preconditions: Non-production object with a known authorized baseline.
tests.procedure: Introduce a reversible out-of-band security change; observe detection, containment decision and reconciliation.
tests.expected: Drift changes technical compliance status and alerts the owner; incident containment is not silently reverted.
tests.evidence: Drift event, policy generation and recovery journal.

tests.title: Platform/provider upgrade regression
tests.preconditions: Exact old/new tuples, release notes and canary tenant.
tests.procedure: Run the applicable suite against the new tuple, including create/update/import/delete and failure paths; evaluate rollback or forward repair.
tests.expected: No mandatory outcome regresses; the new certification is approved before broad placement.
tests.evidence: Tuple manifest, test reports, limitations and promotion decision.

tests.title: Portable contract and object identity
tests.preconditions: Same versioned request and two independently qualified adapters.
tests.procedure: Validate stable consumer fields and compile for both targets; compare semantic outputs without requiring matching topology or vendor IDs.
tests.expected: Equivalent mandatory intent is preserved; unsupported capabilities reject placement rather than silently degrade.
tests.evidence: Normalized requests, adapter plans and semantic comparison.

tests.title: Admission and authorization negatives
tests.preconditions: Schema/profile registry and scoped test identities.
tests.procedure: Submit unknown fields, unresolved profile versions, forged approval references, foreign-tenant references and consumer-supplied status.
tests.expected: All invalid or unauthorized requests are rejected before any allocation or provider action.
tests.evidence: Admission decisions and zero-side-effect audit.

tests.title: Unsupported capability and expired certification
tests.preconditions: Candidate and expired platform profiles.
tests.procedure: Request dual-stack, inspection or dedicated placement on a profile lacking that qualified capability.
tests.expected: Placement fails with an actionable capability reason; candidate/expired records cannot authorize production.
tests.evidence: Placement decisions, capability digests and status.

tests.title: Ownership, quota and separation of duties
tests.preconditions: Tenant quotas and identity/control-plane roles are defined.
tests.procedure: Test permitted workload operations and forbidden foundation/edge/profile edits; race two allocations against the same quota.
tests.expected: Only allowed roles succeed; quota reservation is atomic; no resource is created above a hard entitlement.
tests.evidence: Authorization matrix, concurrent request results and allocation journal.

tests.title: Security-label integrity
tests.preconditions: Provider-owned selectors and tenant-editable labels are distinguishable.
tests.procedure: Attempt to add/remove security labels, impersonate another group or move a workload to a privileged selector.
tests.expected: Tenant changes cannot expand effective permissions; mandatory policy precedence is preserved.
tests.evidence: RBAC results, label audit and effective-rule evaluation.

tests.title: Same-domain east-west isolation
tests.preconditions: Two WSDs deliberately share one approved Security Domain Instance.
tests.procedure: Test same-subnet and cross-subnet traffic with and without explicit FlowIntent; verify traffic on one hypervisor as well as between hosts.
tests.expected: Unapproved east-west communication is denied; allowed flows and required local services function.
tests.evidence: Enforcement location, probes and applied policy.

tests.title: Spoofing and virtual NIC controls
tests.preconditions: Provider-approved packet tests on dedicated non-production endpoints.
tests.procedure: Exercise incorrect source addressing, unauthorized address pairs and additional NIC attachments within the bounded test plan.
tests.expected: Source identities cannot impersonate another domain; platform exceptions have explicit owners and expiration.
tests.evidence: Port/NIC policy, bounded test output and exception records.

tests.title: Shared edge-attachment isolation
tests.preconditions: Two domains use an intentionally shared provider attachment network.
tests.procedure: Exercise direct same-segment paths, ARP/ND interaction, external gateway routing and NAT hairpin in both directions.
tests.expected: No path bypasses per-domain identity and ZIP enforcement; otherwise the shared attachment is ineligible.
tests.evidence: Attachment topology, neighbor state, routes and bidirectional probes.

tests.title: Stateful symmetry and policy routing
tests.preconditions: Multiple eligible edge paths and asymmetric-failure scenario.
tests.procedure: Verify forward/return ownership before and during failover; change PBR to a permitted alternative in the test environment.
tests.expected: Stateful enforcement remains correct; unsupported asymmetry is denied, not resolved by permissive bypass.
tests.evidence: Session traces, PBR precedence and HA counters.

tests.title: Zone adjacency and joint authority
tests.preconditions: Versioned zone graph and authority registry.
tests.procedure: Submit prohibited adjacencies, RZ public attachment, REZ without partner agreement, and a ZIP without both authority approvals.
tests.expected: Invalid graphs are rejected; valid bindings resolve to the explicitly authorized adjacent domains.
tests.evidence: Graph decision report and approval provenance.

tests.title: MZ, OOB and remote administration
tests.preconditions: Approved management architecture and recovery credentials.
tests.procedure: Trace remote privileged access through its authorized boundary; test workload isolation, ordinary browsing restriction and BMC access controls.
tests.expected: MZ semantics and OOB transport remain distinct; only approved privileged paths reach management targets.
tests.evidence: Management diagrams, endpoint policy and session audit.

tests.title: Break-glass and identity-provider loss
tests.preconditions: Approved emergency identity, dual-custodian procedure and test window.
tests.procedure: Make normal federation unavailable; exercise limited emergency access, alerting, revocation and post-use credential rotation.
tests.expected: Access remains accountable and scoped; no shared anonymous administrator or permanent bypass is created.
tests.evidence: Emergency access log, custodial approval and revocation evidence.

tests.title: Workload identity and certificate lifecycle
tests.preconditions: Scoped service identity, trusted CA and rotatable certificate.
tests.procedure: Rotate credentials/certificates; revoke the old identity and test an expired/untrusted certificate.
tests.expected: Approved service continues with new material; old/revoked credentials are unusable within the accepted propagation interval.
tests.evidence: Issuer records, endpoint TLS results and revocation timeline.

tests.title: IPAM concurrency, overlap and exhaustion
tests.preconditions: Small disposable address pool and approved overlap policy.
tests.procedure: Issue concurrent allocations, exhaust the pool, retry requests and request a conflicting prefix.
tests.expected: One authoritative reservation per allocation; retries are idempotent; exhaustion/unauthorized overlap stops provisioning.
tests.evidence: Allocation ledger, request IDs and conflict decisions.

tests.title: DNS/DHCP lifecycle and reuse
tests.preconditions: Forward/reverse zones, address lease policy and reusable test address.
tests.procedure: Provision, rename, recover and retire a network endpoint; confirm lease/DNS reconciliation and address quarantine.
tests.expected: No duplicate active ownership or premature reuse; stale records disappear within the approved timing profile.
tests.evidence: DNS/DHCP/IPAM timelines and ownership comparisons.

tests.title: IPv6 local control and IPv4-only posture
tests.preconditions: Platform offers either a dual-stack or explicit IPv4-only profile.
tests.procedure: Check router advertisements, neighbor discovery, DHCPv6, source validation and unapproved transition paths; preserve required ICMPv6.
tests.expected: No alternate-protocol bypass; enabled IPv6 works correctly and disabled service does not create ungoverned reachability.
tests.evidence: Protocol-specific controls, probes and qualification result.

tests.title: MTU and path-MTU discovery
tests.preconditions: Known encapsulation stack and both local/remote paths.
tests.procedure: Test supported workload packet sizes end-to-end, including security edge, nested overlay if offered and recovery site.
tests.expected: Accepted MTU is reachable without silent black holes; required PMTU feedback is delivered or a documented alternative works.
tests.evidence: Packet-size matrix, encapsulation budget and loss traces.

tests.title: BGP and EVPN import/export boundaries
tests.preconditions: Provider-owned non-production peers and known approved routes.
tests.procedure: Validate neighbor authentication/control-plane limits; advertise bounded unauthorized test prefixes/route targets through the test fixture.
tests.expected: Only authorized advertisements install; route leaks, excess prefixes and unapproved defaults are rejected and alerted.
tests.evidence: Neighbor config, route-policy results and RIB/FIB diff.

tests.title: Leaf/link and multihoming failures
tests.preconditions: Approved MLAG or EVPN multihoming profile; topology-specific rollback.
tests.procedure: Fail an uplink, peer link, keepalive or Ethernet-segment member individually, then restore it; test split-brain containment.
tests.expected: No loop, unintended duplicate forwarding or security bypass; measured convergence meets the fabric profile.
tests.evidence: Fault timeline, MAC/route state, packet-loss and control-plane telemetry.

tests.title: Compute co-residency and evacuation
tests.preconditions: Placement policy names tenant/domain/zone host-sharing boundaries.
tests.procedure: Attempt disallowed placement and evacuate a host; repeat after a scheduler restart.
tests.expected: Placement, migration and HA restart all preserve the approved co-residency rules; insufficient eligible capacity rejects the action.
tests.evidence: Scheduler decisions, host inventory and policy references.

tests.title: Hypervisor and firmware baseline
tests.preconditions: Supported hardware/software tuple and security baseline.
tests.procedure: Verify secure boot/attestation where required, disabled unnecessary services, administrative separation and inventory of firmware/drivers.
tests.expected: All mandatory baseline items are enforced; unsupported or unattested hosts are ineligible for the affected profile.
tests.evidence: Baseline report, attestation/config output and exception ledger.

tests.title: Storage tenant isolation
tests.preconditions: Two tenants with block/file/object resources and separate access identities.
tests.procedure: Attempt foreign volume attachment, snapshot clone, file access and object access; include backup/export paths.
tests.expected: Only the owning or explicitly authorized scope accesses data; no clone or mount circumvents zone/categorization policy.
tests.evidence: API decisions, storage ACLs and data-path tests.

tests.title: Encryption, key isolation and KMS outage
tests.preconditions: Qualified cryptographic profile; disposable encrypted data and test key.
tests.procedure: Validate encryption context and key-use permissions; rotate a test key and remove KMS connectivity under the approved runbook.
tests.expected: No unauthorized decrypt or plaintext fallback; documented cache/restart behavior matches policy; recovery preserves authorized data.
tests.evidence: Crypto configuration, key audit, outage timeline and recovery test.

tests.title: Storage performance and contention
tests.preconditions: Defined capacity/latency/throughput class and bounded load generators.
tests.procedure: Measure steady load, contention and rebuild/degraded state with the same workload data pattern.
tests.expected: Class limits and protected minimums hold under the accepted failure budget; overload rejects growth rather than bypassing controls.
tests.evidence: Latency percentiles, IOPS/throughput, capacity and noisy-neighbor results.

tests.title: Golden image provenance
tests.preconditions: Approved image digest, build manifest and denied image fixture.
tests.procedure: Verify signature/provenance, scan status, boot mode and hardening; attempt deployment of retired/tampered images.
tests.expected: Only eligible images deploy; exceptions are explicit; rebuild output links to its source and component inventory.
tests.evidence: Image manifest, signature validation, scan and admission decisions.

tests.title: Patch and vulnerability lifecycle
tests.preconditions: Inventory, severity policy and an approved non-production patch scenario.
tests.procedure: Create a finding, classify exposure, execute canary remediation, verify fix and record time against the selected deadline.
tests.expected: No asset or firmware layer is omitted; overdue risk escalates; roll-forward/rollback preserves service and security.
tests.evidence: Finding-to-change-to-verification chain and deadline report.

tests.title: Supply-chain and package provenance
tests.preconditions: Approved provider/module mirror and a tampered package fixture.
tests.procedure: Verify package checksums, immutable module references and execution image; test rejection of an unapproved provider/module source.
tests.expected: Tampered/unapproved artifacts never reach a privileged apply; lockfile changes require reviewed provenance.
tests.evidence: Package manifests, verification output and CI policy decision.

tests.title: Terraform plan and state confidentiality
tests.preconditions: Disposable secrets and restricted plan/state storage.
tests.procedure: Inspect source, logs, binary/JSON plan and state using controlled test values; verify supported ephemeral/write-only behavior.
tests.expected: Secrets are absent where promised; unavoidable secret-bearing artifacts remain encrypted, access-controlled and redacted from logs.
tests.evidence: Secret-handling scan, backend ACLs and artifact classification.

tests.title: State locking, recovery and grants
tests.preconditions: Two authorized runners, versioned state and documented lock recovery.
tests.procedure: Race updates to one state, restore a known state version in isolation and test a workload runner against foundation state.
tests.expected: Only one writer operates; restore is auditable; unauthorized state reads/writes fail; state rollback is not misrepresented as resource rollback.
tests.evidence: Lock timeline, recovery report and access decisions.

tests.title: Partial apply and compensation
tests.preconditions: Disposable multi-stage deployment and a failure-injection point.
tests.procedure: Interrupt after allocation or one provider action; restart with the same operation ID and observe discovery/repair.
tests.expected: No duplicate allocation or accidental destruction; unfinished resources remain quarantined; the journal supports safe resume or controlled compensation.
tests.evidence: Operation journal, state generations and residual-resource scan.

tests.title: Retries, optimistic concurrency and idempotency
tests.preconditions: Controller accepts request ID and expected resource generation.
tests.procedure: Replay an operation, submit stale updates, and interrupt response delivery after successful allocation.
tests.expected: Replay returns the existing operation; stale updates conflict; one desired generation yields one accountable realization.
tests.evidence: API responses, generation history and allocation counts.

tests.title: API rate limit and backpressure
tests.preconditions: Finite controller queue and test provider throttling.
tests.procedure: Increase authorized test demand to the configured limit; inject retryable throttling/timeouts and permanent errors.
tests.expected: Backpressure is visible and bounded; retry honors policy/jitter; permanent errors do not loop indefinitely or consume unbounded capacity.
tests.evidence: Queue metrics, retries, deadlines and final operation states.

tests.title: Approved-plan freshness
tests.preconditions: Signed plan, immutable inputs and an intervening policy or state change.
tests.procedure: Change state generation, policy bundle or approval-sensitive intent after planning; try to apply the old artifact.
tests.expected: Stale/unapproved plans are rejected and replanned; approved artifacts bind source, inputs, policy, identity and expiration.
tests.evidence: Plan digest, approvals and rejected apply audit.

tests.title: Evidence integrity and authorization separation
tests.preconditions: Signed evidence manifest and separately signed authorization decision.
tests.procedure: Tamper with an artifact; expire a decision; fail a technical test while preserving the historical authorization record.
tests.expected: Tampering is detected; technical status never self-issues authorization; readiness follows current evidence and decision conditions.
tests.evidence: Digests/signature checks, readiness evaluation and decision history.

tests.title: Telemetry outage, buffering and retention
tests.preconditions: Logging profile specifies export latency, buffer limits and retention/disposal policy.
tests.procedure: Disconnect the collector; generate bounded events; restore connectivity and reconcile sequence/time gaps.
tests.expected: Loss/overflow is alerted; buffering behavior matches profile; mandatory evidence gaps are visible; no silent control bypass.
tests.evidence: Buffer metrics, event reconciliation and retention configuration.

tests.title: Backup administrative separation and immutability
tests.preconditions: Test backup policy includes an isolated locked copy.
tests.procedure: Try deletion or retention reduction with production and backup-operator identities; test approved custodial operations separately.
tests.expected: Compromised production authority cannot alter the protected copy or its retention; authorized actions are separately accountable.
tests.evidence: Role tests, object-lock/immutability configuration and audit.

tests.title: Application-consistent isolated restore
tests.preconditions: Known application dataset, consistency markers and accepted RTO/RPO.
tests.procedure: Restore to an isolated recovery domain; verify integrity, application start and required dependencies before controlled reconnection.
tests.expected: Recovered data meets consistency/RPO and recovery timing; no production connection appears until authorized.
tests.evidence: Recovery timestamps, integrity markers, application checks and isolation probes.

tests.title: Backup retention, holds and key survival
tests.preconditions: A test hold, expiring backup and keys needed by retained copies.
tests.procedure: Retire the WSD while retaining the held copy; attempt key deletion and validate an authorized restore of retained data.
tests.expected: Hold and retention are enforced; key lifetime supports required recovery; data is not prematurely destroyed.
tests.evidence: Hold/retention decision, key dependencies and restore evidence.

tests.title: Site loss, fencing and failback
tests.preconditions: Two qualified sites; isolated exercise scope and owner-approved recovery plan.
tests.procedure: Declare simulated primary loss, fence writers, restore/promote at recovery site, verify DNS/identity/policy, then perform controlled failback.
tests.expected: No split-brain or policy relaxation; measured RTO/RPO and data ownership match the recovery profile.
tests.evidence: Failure timeline, fencing proof, replication checkpoints and end-to-end tests.

tests.title: Management/control-plane bootstrap recovery
tests.preconditions: Offline recovery manifest and independent access to state, DNS/time, trust and keys.
tests.procedure: Recover essential management/controller services in the documented dependency order in an isolated environment.
tests.expected: Recovery does not require the unavailable production service it is restoring; credentials and old state remain accountable.
tests.evidence: Dependency graph, recovery steps, integrity checks and measured recovery time.

tests.title: Resource and address capacity exhaustion
tests.preconditions: Hard quotas, reservations and admission thresholds.
tests.procedure: Exhaust test compute/storage/edge context/address capacity, then request both ordinary and dedicated service classes.
tests.expected: Requests stop with an explicit reason; required HA/security headroom is not consumed or silently weakened.
tests.evidence: Reservation ledger, rejected decisions and remaining-headroom report.

tests.title: Incident quarantine and reconciler precedence
tests.preconditions: Scoped incident role and expiring emergency override.
tests.procedure: Quarantine one WSD, remove exposure and run normal reconciliation; test unaffected tenants.
tests.expected: Containment persists under higher-priority incident policy until released; unrelated tenants remain available.
tests.evidence: Override object, effective policy, reconciliation audit and tenant probes.

tests.title: Exception approval and expiry
tests.preconditions: Versioned exception with risk owner, affected requirement and end time.
tests.procedure: Test unapproved, expired and valid exceptions; expire one during a running operation.
tests.expected: No unapproved exception grants access; expiry changes posture and triggers the documented action without indiscriminate destruction.
tests.evidence: Approval records, admission results and expiry event.

tests.title: Data sanitization and resource reuse
tests.preconditions: Disposable data, snapshot/clone inventory and approved media method.
tests.procedure: Retire the storage object, verify retained copies, sanitize according to the approved method and allocate to another test tenant.
tests.expected: New tenant cannot recover prior data; retained evidence identifies method, scope, exceptions and all surviving copies.
tests.evidence: Sanitization receipt, reuse test and copy/dependency ledger.

tests.title: Portability and exit rehearsal
tests.preconditions: Two target profiles plus an exit manifest containing data and application dependencies.
tests.procedure: Export/rebuild the workload, convert only supported formats, import data and rebind identity/network/keys; run functional and security checks.
tests.expected: Consumer semantics survive; downtime, data loss, format limitations and cost drivers are recorded; no untested live-migration claim.
tests.evidence: Exit manifest, conversion logs, reconciliation report and conformance results.

tests.title: Location, privacy and support access
tests.preconditions: PlacementProfile states permitted data, backup, telemetry, key and administrative locations.
tests.procedure: Compare all components and support paths to those constraints; test a placement or support session outside allowed scope.
tests.expected: Nonconforming placement/access is rejected; exceptions require the designated authority; residency is not asserted to settle jurisdiction.
tests.evidence: Location inventory, access logs and approval decisions.

tests.title: Shared responsibility and control inheritance
tests.preconditions: System control profile, service ownership and inheritance declarations.
tests.procedure: For each applicable control, identify provider, tenant or shared implementation, evidence and unresolved dependency.
tests.expected: No control is ownerless; inherited evidence is scoped, current and accepted; gaps block required readiness.
tests.evidence: Control allocation matrix and assessor review.

tests.title: Public certificate and trusted proxy identity
tests.preconditions: Approved ingress with backend encryption and trusted proxy policy.
tests.procedure: Rotate the certificate, test expiry/incorrect hostname and submit forged client-identity headers through the controlled test client.
tests.expected: TLS identity is validated; backend trust is explicit; untrusted headers cannot impersonate the originating client.
tests.evidence: TLS checks, proxy policy and attributed requests.

tests.title: Egress policy and service-specific protocols
tests.preconditions: Approved egress service includes protocol, destination and DNS resolution policy.
tests.procedure: Test permitted and nearby disallowed destinations; verify NAT identity logs and stateful return traffic.
tests.expected: Only approved egress semantics work; DNS/FQDN changes cannot silently widen policy; NAT is not treated as a security control by itself.
tests.evidence: Egress rules, DNS resolution history, NAT mappings and probes.

tests.title: Privileged workload and container isolation
tests.preconditions: A container/bare-metal profile with explicit isolation capabilities.
tests.procedure: Test namespace/project boundaries, node access, privileged workloads and host-network access against the approved baseline.
tests.expected: Unapproved privilege escalation or host access is denied; namespace alone is not accepted as a qualified zone boundary.
tests.evidence: Admission/RBAC policy, runtime posture and cross-scope tests.

tests.title: Policy precedence and immutable baseline
tests.preconditions: Mandatory provider rules plus lower-priority tenant and service rules.
tests.procedure: Compile overlapping allow/deny intents and update membership while a test workload is running.
tests.expected: Mandatory denies cannot be overridden by tenant policy; membership changes do not create a transient unrestricted interval.
tests.evidence: Effective-rule order, membership transitions and timed probes.

tests.title: ZIP sensors, heightened posture and authority
tests.preconditions: ZIP profile identifies both zone authorities, inspection/sensor policy and heightened mode.
tests.procedure: Verify access-control and telemetry placement; activate heightened posture, test essential flows and restore under approved authority.
tests.expected: Posture change restricts intended flows, preserves declared essentials, and leaves a complete joint-authority record.
tests.evidence: ZIP profile, sensor coverage, change approval and test traces.

tests.title: Time synchronization and correlation
tests.preconditions: Approved independent time sources and skew threshold.
tests.procedure: Measure time across hosts, controllers, edge and collectors; introduce bounded skew in a disposable node.
tests.expected: Excess skew is detected; certificate/evidence validation follows defined failure behavior; record ordering remains explainable.
tests.evidence: Skew metrics, alerts and signed/ordered event samples.

tests.title: Technical readiness gate
tests.preconditions: Healthy and deliberately failed evidence fixtures at the same desired generation.
tests.procedure: Evaluate readiness with missing/expired evidence, unsupported capability, unresolved owner and absent authorization.
tests.expected: Service Ready is false unless every mandatory condition for the current generation is satisfied.
tests.evidence: Condition evaluation, policy version and blocked exposure events.

tests.title: Contract upgrades and deletion finalizers
tests.preconditions: Objects at old schema version; shared domain has two dependent WSDs.
tests.procedure: Convert schema with explicit defaults; delete one WSD; test removal with outstanding retention/evidence finalizers.
tests.expected: No silent security expansion; shared resources survive while referenced; deletion cannot bypass approved finalizers.
tests.evidence: Conversion diff, ownership graph and tombstones.

tests.title: Foundation stability for overlay lifecycle
tests.preconditions: Commissioned overlay capacity and physical fabric configuration snapshot.
tests.procedure: Create, update and retire a routine overlay WSD; compare leaf/spine configuration before and after.
tests.expected: No per-WSD switch change occurs; physical-capacity growth is classified as a separate foundation operation.
tests.evidence: Switch config digests, service class and operation audit.

tests.title: Bare-metal/fabric-routed service boundary
tests.preconditions: Explicit fabric-routed service class and authorized foundation workflow.
tests.procedure: Provision a test physical attachment under separate authority; inspect VRF/RT/interface ownership and retire it.
tests.expected: Consumer contract remains portable; exceptions to overlay workflow are explicit; no unrestricted cross-domain route is introduced.
tests.evidence: Service-class declaration, foundation change and isolation tests.

tests.title: Image/data export compatibility
tests.preconditions: Supported boot mode, drivers, virtual hardware and encrypted-disk context.
tests.procedure: Recreate the workload on the target with a test image; verify guest drivers, time, certificates, application checks and unsupported device handling.
tests.expected: Incompatibilities reject the selected exit path; data/identity are not assumed portable merely because a disk file converts.
tests.evidence: Compatibility checklist, boot logs, application and security tests.

tests.title: Procured-capacity and service inventory reconciliation
tests.preconditions: Procurement/asset inventory, installed capacity and tenant reservations.
tests.procedure: Reconcile ordered, received, staged, commissioned, available, reserved and consumed quantities with accountable owners.
tests.expected: No orphaned or double-counted capacity; unused procured capacity and support expiry are visible for planning.
tests.evidence: Inventory reconciliation and allocation/age report.

tests.title: Document and catalogue completeness
tests.preconditions: Handbook source, schemas, examples, requirements and tests in the release package.
tests.procedure: Check unique IDs, full original-ID migration, references, source links, test mappings, schema validation and generated catalogue parity.
tests.expected: No missing or dangling item; counts and release digest agree; document status does not claim unexecuted platform tests passed.
tests.evidence: Package validation report and manifest.

tests.title: External partner agreement and revocation
tests.preconditions: ExternalDomain has trust basis, authenticated endpoints and named agreement owner.
tests.procedure: Admit an approved binding, then revoke the agreement and check active/new session handling under its profile.
tests.expected: Revocation removes intended access within the agreed interval; no REZ assumption is inferred merely from a private circuit.
tests.evidence: Agreement revision, revocation event and connectivity checks.

tests.title: Flow revocation and live session semantics
tests.preconditions: Approved long-lived test flow with a revocation profile.
tests.procedure: Revoke permission and measure established sessions, cached policies and newly attempted sessions across enforcement points.
tests.expected: New sessions are denied immediately upon committed policy; existing sessions are terminated or drained within the explicitly approved interval.
tests.evidence: Rule generation timeline, session table and probes.

tests.title: Storage clone, snapshot and export classification
tests.preconditions: Protected test volume with snapshot and clone operations enabled.
tests.procedure: Attempt cross-zone clone/export and a lower-categorization target using both tenant and service identities.
tests.expected: Data copies preserve classification and key/access constraints; unapproved downgrade or public export is denied.
tests.evidence: Copy lineage, target checks, key references and audit.

tests.title: Provider/support access time limit
tests.preconditions: Support role, approved session and export/logging rules.
tests.procedure: Open a time-bound support session, test scoped capabilities, expire it and verify all delegated grants are revoked.
tests.expected: No unattended permanent privileged access remains; transferred diagnostics follow approved location and redaction rules.
tests.evidence: Session record, approval, scope tests and revocation receipts.

tests.title: Distributed ZIP equivalence
tests.preconditions: A proposed distributed-enforcement profile and the required ZIP function list.
tests.procedure: Map every required boundary function to its actual enforcement/control component; test same-host and bypass paths plus controller/agent failure.
tests.expected: Logical ZIP semantics are fully met; missing inspection, attribution, failure isolation or authority support rejects qualification.
tests.evidence: Function coverage, topology, policy and fault-test evidence.

addenda.title: Independent native domain routing
addenda.procedure: For the selected stack, enumerate native connected/distributed routes, defaults, provider/external attachments and upstream advertisements. Exercise the approved flow and its forbidden direct alternatives in both directions.
addenda.expected: Only the approved logical ZIP path is usable; native forwarding cannot bypass it.
addenda.safety: Execute only within an authorized representative test environment or explicitly approved production safety envelope.

addenda.title: NSX isolated upstream reference
addenda.procedure: Verify the exact Tier-1, parent/VRF Tier-0, Edge and uplink topology. Review all route propagation and any inter-VRF leaking. Repeat through Edge failure and established-session changes.
addenda.expected: Independent domains remain isolated; the approved stateful path and session behaviour match the profile.
addenda.safety: Execute only within an authorized representative test environment or explicitly approved production safety envelope.

addenda.title: Nutanix external attachment reference
addenda.procedure: Check external subnet connected paths, gateway reachability, NAT/no-NAT behaviour and return routing for each domain. Include neighbours and both offered address families.
addenda.expected: Sharing physical transport does not create direct VPC-to-VPC or workload-to-management access.
addenda.safety: Execute only within an authorized representative test environment or explicitly approved production safety envelope.

addenda.title: OpenStack backend and authority reference
addenda.procedure: Verify chosen backend, Neutron policy, mandatory port/group controls, internal distributed routing and any floating/provider-network alternatives. Recheck after relocation.
addenda.expected: Tenant operations cannot remove mandatory isolation, create an unapproved external path or bypass the intended boundary.
addenda.safety: Execute only within an authorized representative test environment or explicitly approved production safety envelope.

addenda.title: Physical and platform overlay demarcation
addenda.procedure: Verify platform tunnel reachability and effective MTU, fabric route/EVPN imports, multihoming failure and vendor handoff. Document all physical versus logical separation assumptions.
addenda.expected: Fabric interoperability does not import tenant routes or federate vendor overlays outside approved scope.
addenda.safety: Execute only within an authorized representative test environment or explicitly approved production safety envelope.

addenda.title: Bootstrap ownership transition
addenda.procedure: Recover initial access using only the declared independent bootstrap material. Transition to steady-state identity/tooling; revoke temporary credentials and recheck access.
addenda.expected: No circular recovery dependency or untracked residual bootstrap privilege remains.
addenda.safety: Execute only within an authorized representative test environment or explicitly approved production safety envelope.

addenda.title: Composite provider authority
addenda.procedure: Provision one environment using the hosting, edge and name/address/protection scopes. Demonstrate each identity is denied changes outside its package and a downstream failure is recoverable.
addenda.expected: Coordination does not create a shared all-powerful state/identity or destroy shared/data resources on failure.
addenda.safety: Execute only within an authorized representative test environment or explicitly approved production safety envelope.

addenda.title: Persistent platform versus temporary transfer networks
addenda.procedure: Exercise supported live mobility/replication on provider transport and independently activate/expire a bounded cross-domain transfer connection.
addenda.expected: Persistent platform operation remains within its authority; temporary transfer access is removed without dismantling platform foundations.
addenda.safety: Execute only within an authorized representative test environment or explicitly approved production safety envelope.

addenda.title: Brownfield non-destructive adoption
addenda.procedure: Inventory an authorized representative existing scope, confirm single configuration ownership, import/adopt and review the initial plan before mutation.
addenda.expected: No unapproved replacement or competing writer is introduced; adoption does not falsely assert compliance.
addenda.safety: Execute only within an authorized representative test environment or explicitly approved production safety envelope.

addenda.title: Activation sequencing
addenda.procedure: Observe resource creation from reservation through denied network attachment, mandatory controls, internal checks and explicit exposure activation. Introduce a controlled failed activation check.
addenda.expected: No unprotected creation window; failed activation withdraws exposure while preserving data-safe recovery.
addenda.safety: Execute only within an authorized representative test environment or explicitly approved production safety envelope.

addenda.procedure: Inspect actual host, management, storage/controller and transport sharing against adopted source tailoring. Test evacuation and copy operations without relying on labels alone.
